chunk_map.heading: How we work in this room

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent that never resolves strands the reader — absent here. 'the loop' coined ch1 (Big Idea prose) reused ch3/ch6; 'the bug'/'trivial bug' ch1 reused ch3/ch6; 'the repo' established ch2 reused ch3; 'the tracker your team reads' ch1 reused ch6; 'a trick' ch5 immediate continuation; 'the prework'/'Module 2' are indefinite/navigational, not dangling definite referents.

Harm: pointing at another file by position strands readers who entered the deck elsewhere — absent. 'the prework at the top of this workbook' (ch2) matches the compendium's own navigational-pointer carve-out verbatim. Pre-reads (ch8) name author+title inline per entry, not positional callback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a stranded 'the X you did' phantom-references a cut beat — no such backward callback construction appears anywhere in the body; this is the training's opening module with nothing prior to call back to.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reveal narrated above its guess breaks the demo beat — no guess/reveal live-demo structure exists in this overview file's body (that shape lives in the lecture/exercise files it links to).
Harm: a slide with only a wait-state or one context-dependent bullet reads as empty — every chunk here carries a full paragraph or a multi-bullet list with standalone claims.

Harm: a header the content contradicts misleads a skimming reader — each header (Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn, How we work in this room, Start here, Key Concepts, Next, Pre-reads before Module 2) is delivered on by its own chunk's content.

Harm: visible tics (banned triples, self-praise, retracted numbers, abstraction stacks, empty verb legs) read as filler on a projected slide — scanned every chunk, found none: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.', no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlative anywhere in body (checked specifically, none), no number-with-retraction, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: maintainer shop-talk (compendium, beat, mood, surface-as-noun, firing, Connections-as-proper-noun) confuses a room reading a wall projection — none of these terms appear in the body (they appear only in the maintainer block, exempt). 'compound' is the training's own defined loop-stage verb, not repo-internal vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, lightly
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold stops signalling importance once every bullet opens with one, burying real handles elsewhere in the file — present here. Chunk 4 ('How we work in this room') bolds all five bullet leads as complete independent sentences with terminal periods ('We are all learners.', 'Do the exercises.', 'Share and discuss.', 'Skip and come back.', 'We finish at different times.') — the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture shape the rule names by example, distinct from ch3's/ch8's genuine handles (single verbs; 'Read:/Watch: Title' citation labels). Re-derived independently on this re-fire, same finding as the prior fire's TODO. The room-norms maintainer accept-note covers cohort-projection timing only, not this bold shape, so it does not clear the flag.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Bold a short handle per bullet instead of the whole lead sentence, e.g. '**All learners.** Trainers included...' / '**Do the exercises.**' → '**Exercises.** Do them...', or drop bold entirely and let the five stand as plain sentences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against composed deck
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a phase-less prose section can be silently absent from the default Slides view even though it's in long-read — checked site/layouts/slides.js buildDeckModel (lines ~233-282): non-phase module children (Prework, What You'll Learn, Key Concepts, Start here, Next, Pre-reads, How we work in this room) are walked in document order and pushed to `buf`/flushed as prose slides — none dropped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position computed, content ordinals linted
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered Phase/Step headers drift from computed deck position — no such headers exist in this file's body. 'Module 2' references are stable training-level identifiers (M1-M6 numbering), not per-file computed section ordinals, so they're outside this rule's target.
